IV PEDESTRIAN AND BICYLE ACCESS
In the Draft report, it is stated that it is planned that much of the pedestrian traffic will be carried by facilities other than at-grade crosswalks. Therefore, pedestrians generally are considered qualitatively rather than quantitatively. However in the project area, all the existing pedestrian movements are at grade, on sidewalks, including both sides of Main Street, Longfellow Bridge, Third Street, the Badger Building, the DOT building area within the renewal area, the Draper Labs and all the MIT buildings. Any effort to create a second level pedestrian circular system in Kendall Square would have difficulty problem matching with the boundary area of at-grade pedestrian circulation. The Final EIR, therefore, should include a circulation plan of pedestrian movement.
Similarly, some graphic evidence concerning bicycle access should also be included in the Final EIR. New street and traffic patterns should make some provisions for bicycle flows and safety.
V AESTHETICS
The Draft EIR has been prepared at the pre-conceptual phase of development and therefore, any attempt to identify adverse aesthetic impact would be inappropriate.
I recognize the fact that the detailed design work which will eventually be needed concerning impacts cannot yet be presented. However, I share the views expressed in the report that mediocre or poor design of the final product could produce a complex which is equal in unsightliness to the present desolation of the project area. In view of this, the CRA commitment to develop a design review procedure is commendable. To ensure both the architectual and environmental acceptability of the future Kendall Square development, the CRA also should establish an interm design review team which should re-evaluate design review procedures, from time to time and should recommend necessary changes, if required. It is my judgement that this approach would further enhance design review procedure and ultimately help increase aesthetic value of the proposed development.
VI OPEN SPACE
Although approximately 2.5 acres of public open space is proposed, the Draft Report reveals that the majority of the space will be an open plaza. No consideration, however, is given to utilize open space for the development of recreational facilities. This should be considered in the Final report.
The final report also should completely document proposed landscape development of the proposed open space. A critical ratio between paved and landscaped areas should be established. Development of a continuous green belt along the periphery of each existing Parcel should also be considered.
VII SEWERACE AND DRAINAGE SYSTEM
The proposed separate sewerage and drainage system is consistent with the City of Cambridge's on-going program.
